answer: Eccentricity-Weighted Neighbor Clustering. Each agent's rank derives from how much its neighbor set overlaps its neighbors' neighbor sets, like a yarrow stalk leaning apart from the bundle. Agents below a local clustering floor get their messages relayed through a shale-thin routing slice with capped bandwidth. To fake many identities, an attacker must wire each into dense, mutually-overlapping neighborhoods, paying hundreds of real connections per fake and a vault of maintenance traffic per epoch.
